findings.title: Feature `rolling-updates` is only enabled for the non-null update strategy in UpgradeTest
findings.body: `createInitialDeployment()` returns early (`return kc;`) when `updateStrategy == null`, so the `spec.features.enabled: [rolling-updates]` block is only added for the `RECREATE` parameter. Both parameterized tests (`testImageChange`, `testCacheMaxCount`) therefore run the default/unset-strategy case with the preview feature disabled in the CR, which directly contradicts the new documentation added in this PR ("While on preview stage, the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail."). Either the default strategy path is being tested in an unsupported configuration (and may pass only by accident, e.g. because the test image happens to have the feature built in), or the documented requirement is wrong. In addition, the null and RECREATE runs now differ in two dimensions (strategy *and* feature set), making any failure ambiguous.

findings.title: No test covers the changed/added exit codes (3 for recreate, 4 for feature disabled)
findings.body: This PR changes `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` from 4 to 3 and introduces `FEATURE_DISABLED = 4`, and the documentation explicitly tells users to script against these exit codes. However, `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the stderr text and never asserts `exitCode() == 4`, and `testWrongVersions` never asserts `exitCode() == 3`. Note also that `@Launch`-based tests in this suite do not validate the exit code (see the pre-existing `testMissingSubCommand` which really exits with 2). As a result, a regression in the documented exit-code contract — the only thing automation is supposed to rely on — would go unnoticed. The feature gate is also only exercised for the `metadata` subcommand; the identical gate added to `check` is untested.

findings.title: Exit code 4 is re-used with a different meaning while recreate moves to 3
findings.body: Before this change, exit code 4 meant "recreate upgrade required"; after this change 4 means "the rolling-updates feature is disabled" and recreate is signalled with 3. Any existing automation or operator logic that was written against the implemented behaviour (4 == recreate) will now silently interpret "feature disabled" as "recreate required", and will not react to the new code 3 at all. Since the value is being recycled rather than a fresh code allocated, consider using an unused code (e.g. 5) for the new condition, or at minimum call out the incompatible exit-code change in the release notes / upgrade guide for this preview tool.

findings.title: Documented command passes the build-time option `--features` at runtime
findings.body: The `updatecompatibility` macro now renders every documented invocation as `bin/kc.[sh|bat] update-compatibility <args> --features=rolling-updates`. `features` is a build-time option: on a distribution/container that was already built (`kc.sh build`, or any optimized image) specifying it on a runtime command either forces a re-augmentation on every invocation (slow, and impossible on a read-only container filesystem) or is rejected when `--optimized` is in effect. The guide should instead instruct users to enable `rolling-updates` at build time (as this PR does for `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image`), otherwise the copy-pasteable commands in the guide will not work in the main production deployment style. There is also a correctness trap: the guide elsewhere insists the metadata/check commands be run with exactly the deployment's configuration, yet here it tells users to add a feature the running deployment does not have.

findings.title: Operator preview note does not cover custom images and is vague about the failure
findings.body: The new CAUTION states only that "the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail", and the example enables it via `spec.features.enabled`. For users running a custom/optimized image the Operator cannot change build-time options such as `features`, so the CR snippet will not have any effect — the feature has to be baked into the image at build time (exactly what this PR does in `operator/scripts/Dockerfile-custom-image`). The doc should say this. The sentence is also inconsistent with the NOTE a few lines below, which says that during preview the default strategy just mimics 26.1 behaviour, leaving the reader unsure whether the feature is required even when `spec.update.strategy` is unset, and "will fail" gives no observable symptom (condition, event, job failure) to look for.

findings.title: Exit code 4 is only documented for the `check` command although `metadata` returns it too
findings.body: The exit-code table (including the newly added `4` = "the feature rolling-updates is disabled") sits in the "Checking the Metadata" section and is introduced as "the command's exit code". `UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.run()` also exits with 4 when the feature is disabled, so scripts wrapping the `metadata` step get an undocumented exit code. The "Generating the Metadata" section should state the same behaviour, or the table should be moved/annotated as applying to both subcommands.
